env.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: A Telegram bot token from @BotFather (looks like "123456789:ABCdefGhIJKlmNoPQRsTUVwxyZ") — message @BotFather on Telegram and run /newbot to create one.

env.name: TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_CHAT_ID
env.description: A numeric chat/group/channel id (e.g. "-1001234567890" for a group/channel, a positive number for a private chat) or a public channel username (e.g. "@mychannel") to send to when a call doesn't specify one explicitly. For a private chat, the target user must have already started a conversation with the bot (sent /start) — a bot cannot message a user cold. For a group or channel, the bot must already be a member (and, for a channel, usually an admin able to post). If this ability is installed under more than one agent and they should default to different chats, set <AGENT_NAME>_TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_CHAT_ID instead (e.g. SUPPORT_TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_CHAT_ID for an agent named 'support') — that agent's own copy of send_telegram_message checks its own override first and only falls back to this shared value when its override isn't set.
